questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to do with the scroll he handed him?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to eat the scroll.

questions.q: What did the scroll taste like?
questions.a: The scroll tasted as sweet as honey.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to go and do?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to go and speak his words to the people of Israel.

questions.q: Who did Yahweh say Ezekiel was being sent to, instead of a people with a difficult language?
questions.a: Yahweh said Ezekiel was being sent to his own people of Israel, not to a foreign people whose language was too difficult to understand.

questions.q: According to Yahweh, if Ezekiel had been sent to a foreign people, how would they have responded to Ezekiel’s words?
questions.a: If Ezekiel had been sent to a foreign people, they would have listened to Ezekiel’s words.

questions.q: How does Yahweh say the people of Israel will respond to Ezekiel’s words?
questions.a: The people of Israel will not be willing to listen to or obey Ezekiel’s words.

questions.q: What has Yahweh done for Ezekiel so that he will not be fearful or discouraged?
questions.a: Yahweh has enabled Ezekiel to be as strong and stubborn against the people as the people have been against Yahweh.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to do with the words he spoke to him?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to take his words into his heart and listen to them carefully.

questions.q: Where did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to go and speak?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to go to the exiles, the people of his own nation, and declare his message to them.

questions.q: What did the great sound behind Ezekiel say to him?
questions.a: The great sound said, “Blessed be the glory of Yahweh from his place!”

questions.q: What other sounds did Ezekiel hear along with the great earthquake?
questions.a: Ezekiel also heard the sound of the wings of the living beings touching each other and the sound of the wheels beside them.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do to Ezekiel as the Spirit carried him away?
questions.a: Yahweh powerfully authorized Ezekiel to declare his message for him, even though Ezekiel felt resentful and angry.

questions.q: What did Ezekiel then do for seven days, and what was his condition?
questions.a: Ezekiel stayed with the exiles for seven days, overwhelmed by all he was experiencing.

questions.q: When did the word of Yahweh come to Ezekiel?
questions.a: The word of Yahweh came to Ezekiel at the end of seven days.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he had made Ezekiel?
questions.a: Yahweh said he had made Ezekiel a watchman for the house of Israel.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen to Ezekiel if he did not warn the wicked person that they would die if they do not cease their sinful lifestyle?
questions.a: If Ezekiel did not warn the wicked person, Yahweh would consider him responsible for the person’s death.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen to Ezekiel if he warned the wicked person about their sinful lifestyle?
questions.a: If Ezekiel did warn the wicked person, then Ezekiel would not be punished.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen to a righteous person who begins to act unjustly?
questions.a: Yahweh said the righteous person who begins to act unjustly would die because of his sin.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen to Ezekiel if he did warn the righteous man who starts acting unjustly?
questions.a: If Ezekiel did warn the previously righteous man, then Ezekiel would save himself from punishment.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to do?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to get up and go out to the valley, where Yahweh would speak to him.

questions.q: What did Ezekiel do when he saw the glory of Yahweh in the valley?
questions.a: When Ezekiel saw the glory of Yahweh, he bowed with his face to the ground.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to do?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to go and shut himself up in his house.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say the Israelite people would do to Ezekiel?
questions.a: Yahweh said the Israelite people would tie Ezekiel with ropes so that he could not go out among them.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say Ezekiel would not be able to do?
questions.a: Yahweh said Ezekiel would be mute and unable to rebuke the people of Israel.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say Ezekiel would be able to do when Yahweh spoke to him?
questions.a: Yahweh said Ezekiel would be able to speak the words Yahweh gives him to speak.

commentary.text: The preparation of the prophet for his work. (Ezek. 3:1-11) His office, as that of a watchman. (Ezek. 3:12-2) The restraining and restoring his speech. (Ezek. 3:22-27)

Ezek. 3:1-11 Ezekiel was to receive the truths of God as the food for his soul, and to feed upon them by faith, and he would be strengthened. Gracious souls can receive those truths of God with delight, which speak terror to the wicked. He must speak all that, and that only, which God spake to him. How can we better speak God's mind than with his words? If disappointed as to his people, he must not be offended. The Ninevites were wrought upon by Jonah's preaching, when Israel was unhumbled and unreformed. We must leave this unto the Divine sovereignty, and say, Lord, thy judgments are a great deep. They will not regard the word of the prophet, for they will not regard the rod of God. Christ promises to strengthen him. He must continue earnest in preaching, whatever the success might be.

Ezek. 3:12-21 This mission made the holy angels rejoice. All this was to convince Ezekiel, that the God who sent him had power to bear him out in his work. He was overwhelmed with grief for the sins and miseries of his people, and overpowered by the glory of the vision he had seen. And however retirement, meditation, and communion with God may be sweet, the servant of the Lord must prepare to serve his generation. The Lord told the prophet he had appointed him a watchman to the house of Israel. If we warn the wicked, we are not chargeable with their ruin. Though such passages refer to the national covenant made with Israel, they are equally to be applied to the final state of all men under every dispensation. We are not only to encourage and comfort those who appear to be righteous, but they are to be warned, for many have grown high-minded and secure, have fallen, and even died in their sins. Surely then the hearers of the gospel should desire warnings, and even reproofs.

Ezek. 3:22-27 Let us own ourselves for ever indebted to the mediation of Christ, for the blessed intercourse between God and man; and a true believer will say, I am never less alone than when thus alone. When the Lord opened Ezekiel's mouth, he was to deliver his message boldly, to place life and death, the blessing and the curse, before the people, and leave them to their choice.
